hook_candidates.text: In 1977, an intact ship sailed alone with dinner still warm on the table.
Seventy-two seconds of signal changed how astronomers scanned the sky forever.
The radar alarm tripped at midnight, pointing toward an empty patch of ocean.
The deepest vault on Earth held fifty records, but zero visitors were allowed inside.
A three-man crew vanished from an island lighthouse without leaving a single trace.
Deep below the Mediterranean floor lies an intact temple no diver was meant to see.
Astronomers logged the exact frequency, yet forty-nine years later the source remains completely silent.
Over twenty miles of ancient stone sat buried beneath coastal sand for a millennium.

beats.text: In 1977, a radio telescope detected a seventy-two second burst from deep space.
Astronomer Jerry Ehman was reviewing computer printouts when a sequence of six letters jumped out.
He grabbed a red pen, circled the code 6EQUJ5, and scribbled 'Wow!' in the paper margin.
The signal peaked at thirty times the background noise of empty space on the hydrogen line.
This exact frequency is protected internationally, meaning terrestrial aircraft and radar transmitters are legally banned from broadcasting on it.
The bell-shaped signal intensity curve matched the precise motion of Earth rotating past an interstellar source.
Astronomers spent forty-seven years scanning that exact patch in Sagittarius, but the cosmos has remained completely silent.
Nearly fifty years later, astronomers still listen for that seventy-two second burst from deep space.
